Subject: Quick recap + concrete next tests after today's demo

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- What we demoed: 1) streaming chat with function/tool calls, 2) per-route autoscaling (dedicated), 3) economic controls (batching & cache knobs).
- Finora concerns raised: pricing delta vs hyperscaler endpoints for high-volume inference, predictable tail latency, and data residency for some EU/US workflows.

Immediate asks we agreed on: 
1) Redwood will run a 1M-token cost comparison using your typical mix (40% chat, 60% embedding-ish requests), with three scenarios: no batching, 8-request batching, and aggressive batching + prefix cache at 30% hit.
2) We'll produce P95 latency plots for each scenario and show fallback behavior under saturated load.
3) Procurement wants a simple runbook showing steps to sign a Dedicated contract and expected provisioning timeline.

I've attached a short spreadsheet draft that outlines the cost model assumptions we used in the demo (redwood_pricing_vs_hyperscaler.xlsx). Please skim and flag any usage-profile changes.

Next step: I propose we deliver the cost/latency artifacts by EOD Mon (23 Nov). Can you confirm the usage mix above and whether procurement wants the contract runbook in parallel?

Thanks,

Adding a couple of internal notes for the sim: 
- Use the Finora mix Alex specified (55/45). For token-length distribution, assume chat median context 1.8k tokens/session, generation median 120 tokens.
- For hyperscaler comparison, we'll use the observable published endpoint rate card plus the additional networking egress assumptions. Hyperscaler numbers tend to understate overhead for KV-cache misses and multi-az replication — let's model a +12% effective token cost for their managed endpoints to account for that.
- For Dedicated provisioning: typical lead time is ~10 business days for first pool in our us-west region but can be cut to 5-7 days with cloud partner fastpath (subject to contract).

I'll spin up an internal sim and drop the token-econ-sim.csv into the shared drive by Friday.

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: alex.chen@finora.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com, procurement@finora.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:18:00 -0800
Subject: Deliverables: cost sim + latency charts (first pass)

Alex / procurement team — attaching first-pass artifacts per our plan. Highlights: 

- 1M-token cost (scenario summary):
  • Redwood (no batching, no cache): $8.9 per 1M tokens
  • Redwood (batch size 8): $3.7 per 1M tokens
  • Redwood (batch 8 + 30% cache): $2.6 per 1M tokens
  • Hyperscaler managed endpoint (modeled): $4.8 per 1M tokens (note: we applied +12% overhead adjustment)

- Latency P95 at 150 rps:
  • Redwood (no batching, cold): 420ms
  • Redwood (batch 8, warmed): 125ms
  • Hyperscaler (modeled, warmed): 210ms

Key callouts: batching yields the largest per-token delta. At high sustained RPS, Redwood's continuous batching + prefix cache reduces unit cost significantly while keeping P95 below the hyperscaler in the warmed path.

Files attached: redwood_pricing_vs_hyperscaler.xlsx, token-econ-sim.csv. Also included a short runbook: Dedicated provisioning steps + expected timelines.

Requested next steps from Finora:
- Procurement: confirm if you want the Dedicated SOW template in Word or PDF (I can send both).
- Platform: confirm you want a deeper test that includes multi-AZ failover and the canary fallback we demoed (we propose a 2-hour load window at 200 rps to validate tails).

If that sounds right I'll schedule the multi-AZ test for next week and get Ben to own the runbook details.

Thanks,
Lauren

Attachment: token-econ-sim.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: soojin.lee@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, alex.chen@finora.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deliverables: cost sim + latency charts (first pass)

Adding the proposed test plan and acceptance criteria — putting it here so procurement/platform have a single source of truth.

Proposed short validation (2-part):
1) Economics & latency run (2 hours)
   - Target sustained load: 200 rps for 2 hours; use Finora 55/45 mix.
   - Scenarios: (A) Redwood warmed with batch=8 + 30% prefix cache; (B) Hyperscaler modeled warmed with same mix.
   - Acceptance: Redwood P95 warmed <= 150ms AND per-1M token cost <= hyperscaler modeled cost by >= 20% OR explain variance.

2) Failure & fallback (30 minutes)
   - Induce transient capacity pressure to trigger canary fallback to a lower-cost compatible model. Verify no more than 2x increase in P95 and no data-loss.

Logistics/notes:
- We will provide an isolated API key and a load script. Finora will point test clients to the dedicated endpoint (or hyperscaler endpoint for their internal run).
- Procurement: to sign Dedicated we need the PO and initial 3-month commit on record; Ben/LAuren will send SOW + SLA doc.

Alex — does the acceptance criteria look reasonable? If yes we'll schedule Wednesday next week and loop procurement to lock the SOW timeline.

—Soojin
